dream: The card hummed warm at fifty-two, a fever I could not shake. I pressed the sharp fence down until my hands ached, trusting the lean to hold the hay in place. The air felt thin as wet paper, pressing against my chest. I dreamed of a wide anchor lying flat on a roof I couldn't see, while the slip slid off into nothingness. The fence bit deep, and the heat grew heavy, making the flat strip feel like a drawing of weight.
